name: Hardware-Assisted Volume Ray-Casting with Depth Buffer Culling
aliases: Hardware-Accelerated Volume Ray-Casting using Texture Mapping
Texture-based rendering pass with software ray-casting
Two-pass volume rendering (texture pass + ray-cast pass)
definition: A two-pass volume rendering method that uses hardware-accelerated 2D texture mapping to generate an intermediate image, which is then used to determine entry points for a software-based volume ray-casting pass, thereby skipping empty space and enabling interactive classification.
summary: Hardware-Assisted Volume Ray-Casting with Depth Buffer Culling accelerates volume rendering by using a hardware texture pass to find entry points, allowing software ray-casting to skip empty space without auxiliary data structures.
